answer: Refraction Ledger. Each identity holds a random point on a shared ledge of challenge coordinates; every action must return a signed response passing through a vertex that only that point yields. Duplicates cannot fake distinct points without colliding on the same vertex, which the ledger detects on the next epoch and flags publicly. The prism of cross-checks between neighbors exposes cloned responses instantly. An attacker must solve and maintain separate valid coordinates per clone, paying full compute and storage per identity.
